title: 1975-11-05_SECTION_013_01.txt
concise_summary: In this letter to Gene Savoy of the International Community of Christ, PKD presents a systematic retrospective account of his March 1974 visionary experience, arguing that the entity he encountered was Hagia Sophia — identified as the Logos and the firstborn of creation — whose presence healed him and accurately diagnosed his infant son's life-threatening birth defect. He then moves into Exegesis-mode journal entries, deploying Aristotelian cosmology (sublunar vs. supralunar realms) and NeoPlatonism to argue that the Christian concept of heaven is literally the band of fixed stars, with grace being the supralunar world's intervention into the sublunar, and that his 2-3-74 experience was an instance of exactly this divine intercession. A secondary strand frames his experience within a theology of cosmic warfare, using Dietrich Bonhoeffer's martyrdom as a parallel to argue that his rescue in March 1974 was part of God's historical war against tyranny — the same war depicted in his novel A Scanner Darkly (TEARS).
key_claims: The entity PKD encountered in 2-3-74 was Hagia Sophia, identifiable as the Logos and firstborn of creation, whose nature is exactly described in the Wisdom of Solomon.

Santa Sophia's prophesied rebirth ('she was not acceptable before') is a hidden identification of Wisdom with Christ, proving the correctness of linking Proverbs 8 and the Book of Wisdom to Christology.
A true mystical body of the Pantocrator exists; the Holy Spirit acts as agent of 'second birth,' transforming the believer into a 'creature of light' (firebright) that will consume the sarx.

Aristotle's sublunar/supralunar distinction, mediated through NeoPlatonism, provides the cosmological framework for Christian heaven: the supralunar realm of fixed stars can enter the sublunar world as grace.

PKD's 2-3-74 experience was not a private mystical event but part of a single cosmic war in which God attacked the tyranny (the Nixon-era conspiracy) and simultaneously rescued its unjustly imprisoned victims.
Sacred knowledge of entry into the mystical corpus of the Pantocrator has been lost for approximately fifteen hundred years and must be recovered.
recurring_concepts: Hagia Sophia / Santa Sophia — divine Wisdom as Logos and firstborn of creation
Pantocrator — the cosmic Christ as head of a living mystical body
Second birth (palingenesis) — Holy Spirit transformation of the believer into a creature of light
Firebright — PKD's term for the newly created inner being of light and fire born within the believer
Sublunar / supralunar cosmology — Aristotelian framework for distinguishing deterministic earth-realm from the free realm of fixed stars
Good Friday Spell — Wagner/Goethe image of the landscape transformed by the presence of the Savior
Mystical corpus / soma of the Pantocrator — the living corporate body of which believers are members
Augenblick — the decisive moment of divine intervention into history
people_entities: Gene Savoy — founder of the International Community of Christ, Reno, Nevada; addressee of the letter
Dietrich Bonhoeffer — German Lutheran pastor and anti-Nazi martyr, used by PKD as a parallel case of martyrdom and divine non-intervention
Aristotle — ancient Greek philosopher; PKD invokes his sublunar/supralunar cosmological distinction
Spinoza — philosopher; cited for the doctrine that God possesses physical extension and is immanent in the universe as its soma
Plato — ancient philosopher; PKD refers to Platonic 'pictures' (cave allegory) to describe normal, limited perception
Plotinus / NeoPlatonists — implied via PKD's reference to NeoPlatonism and the supralunar world reaching into this world as grace
Goethe — German poet; cited for the 'Good Friday Spell' image of the landscape transformed
Wagner — German composer; cited alongside Goethe for the 'Good Friday Spell' (from Parsifal)
Luke (Evangelist) — PKD identifies the Greek he heard as specifically Luke's Greek New Testament language
Paul (Apostle) — cited for the term sarx (flesh), which the creature of light will consume
Jesus / Christ — the Savior whose return is prophesied by Hagia Sophia's statement; identified with Sophia/Logos
Christopher Dick — PKD's infant son, whose inguinal hernia (birth defect) was diagnosed by Hagia Sophia through PKD and required surgery
Sarapis — Hellenistic mystery-religion deity; cited as an example of god-as-liberator parallel to Christ
texts_works: The Wisdom of Solomon (Apocrypha) — PKD finds in it an exact description of Hagia Sophia as the entity who entered him
Colossians 1:13 (New Testament) — quoted for 'He is the head of the body' and the Pantocrator passage about the universe being created through and for Christ
Proverbs 8 (Hebrew Bible) — linked to Sophia/Wisdom tradition and identified with Christ
Luke (New Testament) — the specific Greek PKD heard was identified as Luke's
New Testament (Greek) — the language PKD heard in hypnagogic state was New Testament Greek
Fidelio (Beethoven opera) — cited as analogy for the release of unjustly imprisoned prisoners when tyranny is overthrown
A Scanner Darkly (referred to as TEARS) — PKD's novel depicting divine war against tyranny; the scene of intervention is referenced
autobiographical: PKD's 'conversion experience' ran from March 18, 1974 to March 23, 1975 — precisely one year — nineteen months before this letter
The last hypnagogic words PKD heard were 'The Buddha is in the park,' which he interpreted as announcing the Savior's return
The initial four days of the experience felt like gaining sight after blindness; PKD experienced reality 'as it was' rather than as Platonic pictures
PKD had been very ill for almost two years before 2-3-74, bedridden most of the time; the illness ceased when the experience began
PKD heard New Testament Greek in hypnagogic state, which he found to be both religious and healing

Hagia Sophia (speaking through PKD) accurately diagnosed his infant son Christopher's birth defect, urged his wife to take the child to the doctor immediately, and the child required surgery — his life had been in peril since birth
PKD produced approximately 200,000 words of notes and research on his experience before writing this letter
PKD watched a TV program about Dietrich Bonhoeffer that prompted a journal entry connecting his own experience to the theology of martyrdom and divine rescue
In November 1971 PKD experienced an 'attack' that was not defended in the way his March 1974 experience was
After 2-3-74 PKD sat outside at night watching the sky and the stars, sensing their connection to the supralunar realm
PKD placed the phrase 'Santa Sophia will be reborn' in Deus Irae without fully comprehending its theological implications at the time
theological_motifs: Logos — the firstborn of creation, identified with both Sophia and Christ
Theosis / second birth — Holy Spirit transformation of the believer into a creature of light
Hylozoism — the doctrine that God possesses physical extension; Spinoza's immanent God whose universe is His soma
Parousia — the return of the Savior, announced by Hagia Sophia's utterance and signaled by 'The Buddha is in the park'
Mystical body of Christ — the living corporate Pantocrator of which believers are members
Grace — the supralunar world's intervention into the sublunar, described in Aristotelian/NeoPlatonic cosmological terms
Sublunar determinism vs. supralunar freedom — cosmological dualism mapping onto earth/heaven distinction
Good Friday Spell — presence of the transformed Savior perceived in the landscape
Sarx — Pauline flesh/body to be consumed by the creature of light
Martyrdom and divine rescue — theology of when heaven does and does not intervene to save the faithful
Sacred knowledge / gnosis — lost for fifteen hundred years; knowledge of entry into the mystical corpus
Cosmic warfare — God's war against tyranny as the frame for PKD's personal rescue
Adventitious revelation — the phrase about Sophia's rebirth as information PKD could not have known himself
Mystery religions — Hellenistic liberator-gods (Sarapis, Christ) as analogues for divine rescue from bondage
literary_self_ref: PKD states he placed the phrase 'Santa Sophia will be reborn; she was not acceptable before' into Deus Irae without fully comprehending it, retroactively discovering its deep Christological import — framing his fiction as unconscious or inspired prophecy

PKD refers to a 'scene in TEARS' (A Scanner Darkly) depicting the divine attack on tyranny, arguing that novel's imagery directly reflects the cosmic war he experienced in March 1974 — his fiction and his theology are 'of one piece'
symbols_images: The park — hypnagogic image interpreted as the place of the Buddha's birth / the Savior's return
Bells and transformed landscape — the 'Good Friday Spell' signaling the presence of the Savior
Firebright — inner being of fire and light born within PKD, imagined as having come from the stars
Stagnant ocean viewed from above — dream image of the sublunar world seen from the supralunar perspective, with humans as creatures of the ocean
The band of fixed stars / supralunar heaven — literal cosmological location of the divine realm
Fidelio — Beethoven's opera of unjust imprisonment and release, used as image for the logical consequence of defeating tyranny
200,000 words of notes — image of obsessive scholarly accumulation as spiritual method
The night sky — stars watched by PKD after 2-3-74, now understood as the supralunar realm made visible
tensions: PKD identifies the voice as Hagia Sophia but also refers to the experience as tied specifically to Christ and the Good Friday Spell — the relationship between Sophia and Christ is asserted as identity but never rigorously demonstrated within the letter
PKD claims 'The Buddha is in the park' meant the Savior had returned, but this requires eliding the difference between Buddhist and Christian soteriological frameworks in a way he does not address

The cosmic-war theology requires PKD's personal suffering and rescue to be historically significant, but the mechanism connecting his capture to the 'bringing down of the conspiracy' (Watergate/Nixon) is stated rather than explained

PKD admits he placed the Sophia phrase in Deus Irae 'without fully comprehending it,' which complicates his claim that it represents adventitious revelation — was it divinely inspired or accidentally prophetic?

The hylozoistic/Spinozan model (God as immanent soma of the universe) sits in tension with the Aristotelian/NeoPlatonic model (God as supralunar, intervening into sublunar from outside) — PKD does not resolve this duality

PKD states that sacred knowledge of entry into the mystical corpus has been 'lost for fifteen hundred years' but simultaneously implies his experience recovered it — the epistemological status of this recovery is left unresolved
evidence_quotes: "The voice speaking to me, which I had identified as Haggia Sophia, had as its utmost revelation told me, 'Santa Sophia will be born again. She was not acceptable before.'"

"What I have finally come to think, after making my 200,000 words of notes of research and thoughts, is that a true mystical body of the Pantocrator exists, and that the Holy Spirit coming on the original followers of Christ was to cause them to fully experience themselves as parts of this corpus, which was alive, which was completing the universe."
"Saint Sophia through me absolutely accurately diagnosed Christopher's birth defect and told my wife, 'You must take him to the doctor now; don't wait; phone the doctor.'"
"God attacked the powerful and wicked, and He assisted the weak, the victims who had made moral stands. I was lucky. My capture had not come too soon."

"Heaven is the heavens, the realm of fixed stars, or even above ('Ubrem Sternanzelt'). If, during one's lifetime in this the sublunar realm, one finds favor with God, then upon one's death one ascends."
uncertainty_flags: The letter is addressed to Gene Savoy of the International Community of Christ, but the latter portion of the text appears to be private journal entries appended to or following the letter — the exact boundary between epistolary and journal text is unclear from the raw_text

PKD refers to 'TEARS' but the linked_terms confirm this is A Scanner Darkly; scholars should note PKD used 'TEARS' as a working title or internal shorthand and this identification should be verified against other Exegesis entries

'The November 71 attack' is mentioned but not explained — this likely refers to the break-in at PKD's house in November 1971, but the exact nature of this event and PKD's interpretation of it remain ambiguous here
PKD uses 'Haggia Sophia' (double-g spelling) throughout — this may be a consistent personal orthography or a transcription error; the canonical Greek is Hagia Sophia
The raw_text ends mid-sentence ('Could it also be said that the mere phenomenological world which I') — the segment appears truncated; scholarly analysis must account for the incomplete argument

PKD identifies the Greek he heard as 'Luke's' specifically, but offers no philological evidence for this identification — it may reflect post-hoc rationalization rather than real-time linguistic recognition

The phrase 'Ubrem Sternanzelt' appears to be a garbled rendering of 'Uber'm Sternenzelt' (above the starry vault) from Schiller's 'Ode to Joy' as set by Beethoven — PKD does not identify the source, and the misspelling suggests it may be from memory

raw_text: November 5, 1975 Mr. Gene Savoy, International Community of Christ, 100 North Arlington Avenue, Reno, Nevada 89501. Dear Mr. Savoy: Thank you so much for writing me. Yes indeed, I would like to take your study program. Perhaps you could have somebody write me as to costs, etc. It has been nineteen months since my "conversion experience," as my priest calls it, began. It lasted, I discovered to my surprise, almost precisely one year, from March 18, 1974 to March 23, 1975. The last words I heard in hypnagogic state, which is the ASC I heard the most in, was, "The Buddha is in the park." I rushed to my reference sources and of course discovered, as I'm sure you know, that "the park" refers to the place where the Buddha was born. The voice speaking to me, which I had identified as Haggia Sophia, had as its utmost revelation told me, "Santa Sophia will be born again. She was not acceptable before." I had no idea who "Saint Sophia" was, and was astounded to learn that she is the logos, the firstborn of all that was created. That "Saint Sophia" referred to Christ was evident. I was being told, in other words, then, that Christ would return, after having been rejected before. Later, "The Buddha is in the park" I took to mean that in fact the Savior had returned. As to my experience itself, in the initial four days I was seeing in the sense of formerly having been blind, and experiencing reality as it was, rather than pictures (in Plato's sense). I actually thought I had been blind, and so differently did I see and experience the universe that I was never after able to be at home in it, as we normally see, what little part our normal percept system brings to us. I am now deprived of what I experienced almost as that which the hylozoistic philosophers believed in (for example, Spinoza in his doctrine that God possesses the attribute of physical extension, so that in fact He is an immanent God, and the universe is in some way His soma, of which His psych4 is another expression or attribute). But certain portions of my experience were specifically tied in with Christ. (one) The experience took place at the vernal equinox, and probably on or about Christ's actual birthday. (two) I was conscious of bells and a transformation of the landscape, especially the landscape, which both Goethe and Wagner describe as the "Good Friday Spell," in other words meaning that the Savior, in His transformed morphophos, was present. -2- (three) The language I heard turned out to be the Greek of the New Testament, in particular Luke's, and was both religious and healing in nature, which goes with the notion of the Good Friday Spell (let me say at this point that I had been very ill for almost two years, and was bedridden most of the time; this ceased when the experience began). (four) The specific reference to "Saint Sophia." (five) In the book "The Wisdom of Solomon" I have discovered an exact account and description of the very inner nature of this entity which entered me or somehow revealed Itself to me both outside and in­ side. It was indeed Haggia Sophia. (six) a passage in "Colossians" which a person recently brought to my attention: 1:13, in particular: "He is, moreover, the head of the body." And, prior: "The whole universe was created through him and for him. Ana he exists before everything, and all things are held together in him." Anu: "He is the image of the invisible God." We are speaking of the Pantocrator. What I have finally come to think, after making my 200,000 words of notes of research and thoughts, is that a true mystical body of the Pantocrator exists, and that the Holy Spirit coming on the original followers of Christ was to cause them to fully experience themselves as parts of this corpus, which was alive, which was completing the universe, the Holy Spirit being the agent which brought the "second birth" to the person, used him as a receiving entity, and tnen this "second birth" within him, which was a newly made creature of light (I called it within me "firebright," supposing it to be of fire and of light and to have come from the stars, somehow) would grow until it had consumed what Paul called sarx with such distaste. That I was, for four days, within a living universe or entity, which spoke to me and healed me, in the most loving terms — there is no doubt, since it also compelled me to get some medical help for my year-old-son who had a birth defect which the doctor told us "wasn't really there." It required an operation, in fact, and my son's life had beeen in peril from the time of his birth. Saint Sophia through me absolutely accurately diagnosed Christopher's birth defect and told my wife, "You must take him to the doctor now; don't wait; phone the doctor." Surgery was scheduled as soon as possible. Anyhow, enough of this. There is, as "Colossians 1:13" says, a mystical invisible corporate body of which we are the members, but the sacred knowledge of entry into this has been lost probably for fifteen hundred years. Yes indeed, I would like to take study from the ICC. And thank you so for writing me. I had my head buried in research. Cordially, Philip K. Dick 2461 Santa Ysabel Ave Fullerton Calif 92631 Watching the TV program about Dietrich Bonhoffer, I realized that heaven does not usually step in to physically save someone who is about to be a martyr. But in March 1974 heaven had begun (hr had before that) its war against the tyranny, and the other side of the coin was its assistance to the impending martyrdom of someone who had renounced his comfort, his freedom, his career, his future, fled to a foreign country and then returned... the help given me was offered because the Presence of the Lord had "broken through," as shown in TEARS, with His host. Had my capture not coincided with heaven's Augenblick of intervention into history then there would have been no rescue this side of the grave. The two events —the bringing down of the conspiracy, as I was shown— and the help given me were of one piece. God attacked the powerful and wicked, and He assisted the weak, the victims who had made moral stands. I was lucky. My capture had not come too soon. This is why the Nov 71 attack was not "defended," in the sense that there was a defending by the Helper in March 74. As I was caught up in the (moral) war, so I was caught up in the victory, rescued by the celestial victors; but this all puts a new light on the scene in TEARS in reference —not only to the attack on the tyranny— but to the help for me. After all, would not the act of intervention to defeat the tyranny include logically the release (as in "Fidelio") the release of its unjustly injured prisoners and victims? CAN THE TWO ASPECTS BE SEPARATED? This puts my experience in perspective, as a portion of one vast fabric that took place at that time. Aristotle's distinction between the sublunar world and the supralunar world, leading into NeoPlatonism (in the latter it is believed that the supralunar world —the band of fixed stars— can reach down into this world, which would be the same as grace). Determinism rules here; freedom there. This agrees with the mystery religions view of God freeing man (through His intervention, which is to say, grace again; cf the worship of Sarapis et al.). (Christ would be one of these.) Hence I saw in several dreams a viewpoint from above looking down into a stagnant ocean, with us as creatures of that ocean...the sublunar world seen from the supralunar world (above). This agrees with Jesus' "...On earth as it is in heaven," heaven being supralunar, earth being sublunar.
